clue.text: Flask church needed to hold a service

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is said to hold the service, so it wraps round it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A churchgoer needs a flask to see them through a long service.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass bottle for serving wine or water, a kind of flask.

clue.text: Boy served up duck in wine in hot dish

indicators.note: the boy and duck are placed in the wine, so the wine word wraps round them

parts.note: vino is an informal word for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A boy brings duck cooked in wine to the table as a hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads the boy upwards (DAL), which with the duck sits 'in' the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiercely spicy curry, a classic example of a hot dish.

clue.text: Wearing pelt and cape after pub brawl in town

indicators.note: the clothing-and-cape pieces come after the pub and the brawl in the answer

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a noisy fight
in, as in dressed in, means wearing
fur is an animal's pelt
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: Someone in fur and a cape gets caught up in a pub fight in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: BARROW-IN-FURNESS is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is an English port town, so it fits the plain word town.

clue.text: What did you say in loo about French place?

indicators.note: the query is placed in the toilet word, which wraps round it

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a loo
eh? is how you ask someone to repeat themselves
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone shouting from a toilet asks what you said about a place in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a port city in Normandy, so it is a place in France.

clue.text: Comment by Mail showing advanced viewpoint?

parts.note: an observation is a remark or comment
post is mail, letters delivered

explanation.surface: A remark in the Daily Mail reveals an advanced point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mail is a British newspaper, which pulls the surface toward politics.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a forward military position for watching the enemy, an advanced spot to view from.

clue.text: Old toast wife leaves in mug?

indicators.note: the wife is said to leave, so her letter is removed from the toast

parts.note: wassail is an old drinking toast

explanation.surface: An old toast is drunk, and the wife walks out leaving it in a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to attack them in the street, which is to assail them.

clue.text: Most of family group daughter covered

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a clan is a family group

explanation.surface: Nearly all the family huddles round to keep the daughter covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means dressed or covered, as in ivy-clad walls.

clue.text: Port makes singer lose voice quality

indicators.note: the singer is made to lose the quality, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a baritone is a male singer
tone is the quality of a voice

explanation.surface: A port city somehow makes a singer lose the quality of their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a seaport on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Parrot in Andes initially taking exercise

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the mountain range's name is taken

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A parrot in the Andes is out getting some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot someone is to copy them mindlessly, which is to ape them.

clue.text: Black rock band to start with zest — without amps!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the band-and-zest letters stand outside the amps letter
to start with means only the opening letter of the word band is used

parts.note: salt means zest or piquancy, as in the salt of wit
A is the abbreviation for amps, amperes

explanation.surface: A rock band begins playing with zest, but unplugged and without amps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black rock band' tempts toward a group; 'Black rock' is the definition. 'without' means outside, so BSALT wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, so it is a black rock.

clue.text: Butcher's chestnut horse should be returned

indicators.note: returned means the chestnut horse pieces are read backwards

parts.note: chestnut is a reddish brown, so red
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A butcher's chestnut horse ought to be given back.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. REDNAG reads backwards as GANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander, like a butcher's, is slang for a look or glance.

clue.text: Queen, first to appear, slowed down for an audience

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the word appear is taken
for an audience means what follows is heard, not spelt

parts.note: delayed means held up, slowed down

explanation.surface: A queen, first to appear on stage, walks slowly for her audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was the consort of William IV, Queen of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: One supporting Reds on the same train as me?

definitions.meaning: a ... sympathises with communists without joining the party

definitions.text: on the same train as me?
definitions.meaning: literally a fellow passenger on one's journey

explanation.surface: A football fan supporting the Reds is on my train.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a communist sympathiser and, literally, a companion on a journey.

clue.text: Greek goddess banning husband for long time

indicators.note: banning the husband means his letter is excluded from the goddess

parts.note: Hera was queen of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess bans her husband for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Hera's husband Zeus was famously unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, a long time.

clue.text: Out of water — area reduced to dust

parts.note: ground means crushed into powder

explanation.surface: Out of water, the land is reduced to dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground is stuck on the bottom, out of the water it should float in.

clue.text: Wildebeest seen in big numbers

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Wildebeest are seen in big numbers on migration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnu is another name for the wildebeest, an African antelope.

clue.text: Books given to staff showing long seat

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

explanation.surface: Books are given to the staff, who show off a long seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a long low upholstered seat or footstool, often with storage inside.

clue.text: Mother worried about me — that indicates resistance!

indicators.note: about means the jumbled mother letters go round the other word
worried suggests agitated, so the letters of mother are reworked

explanation.surface: A mother worries about me, and that shows she is resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes OHMTER, which goes 'about' the clue's own word. Resistance is electrical, not a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohmmeter is an instrument measuring electrical resistance in ohms.

clue.text: Boxes for example, and got ears bashed

indicators.note: bashed means knocked about, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: He boxes, for instance, and gets a bashing round the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' reads as a boxer's punches; it is the noun for containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxes are containers for keeping things, an example of storage.

clue.text: Scramble up mountain track, perhaps

definitions.note: the comma before this word is the thing defined, an example of the answer

indicators.note: scramble means mix up, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A climber scrambles up a mountain track.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the comma plus 'perhaps': that comma is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is one of several punctuation marks, so the comma here is an example.

clue.text: Partly processed food set in batter?

definitions.note: a noun for something that batters

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings back up to chew again
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: Half-cooked food is set in batter, like a failed recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like a cooking mixture; here it means a thing used to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short heavy club, something used to beat people.

clue.text: Flier blows top, having eaten too much: it's bad

indicators.note: having eaten means the bird holds the next piece inside it
blows top means the bird loses its top letter, the first in a down entry

parts.note: a wren is a small bird, a flier
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A bird loses its temper after overeating, which is bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows top' drops W from WREN, leaving REN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten means very bad, whether decayed or of poor quality.

clue.text: Tale-teller had last Tudor wife coming round

indicators.note: the wife comes round, wrapping herself about the other word

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the last wife of Henry VIII
to be had is to be done, cheated

explanation.surface: A storyteller was conned when Henry VIII's last wife came round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pardoner is one of the pilgrims in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales who tells a story.

clue.text: State to wobble after leader deposed

indicators.note: deposing the leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to waver is to wobble

explanation.surface: A state starts to wobble after its leader is deposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly, to state it.

clue.text: Suddenly others plunged into Italian river

indicators.note: plunged into means the others go inside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Suddenly the others leapt into an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto, as in a conjuror's hey presto, means suddenly or at once.

clue.text: Care in relapse required regularly for old hero

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Care is needed regularly when an old hero relapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeneas is the Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid, a figure of classical legend.

clue.text: Fuel found with short cut

indicators.note: short means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut

explanation.surface: Fuel is found alongside a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' reads as a route; 'short' trims GASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is burnt as a fuel, and in American use is petrol.

clue.text: Waste carrier avoiding small vessel

indicators.note: avoiding means the small letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a sewer carries waste

explanation.surface: A waste carrier avoids a small vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel for water.
